topLine: The Independent Commission Against Corruption has reported on what it describes as a "boys' club" culture within Corrective Services NSW, in which it says sexualised language is tolerated and staff are discouraged from complaining. Elsewhere in state politics, NSW regional and interstate passenger trains face a week-long suspension from Friday because of industrial action, and the Sydney Morning Herald examines Premier Chris Minns' approach to recruiting Labor candidates ahead of 2027. Locally, a Kiama CBD proposal involving the demolition of a heritage-listed property has emerged, and the government is promoting an Illawarra Shoalhaven paramedic pilot it says has kept more than 1200 people out of emergency departments.

Elsewhere in state politics, NSW regional and interstate passenger trains face a week-long suspension from Friday because of industrial action, and the Sydney Morning Herald examines Premier Chris Minns' approach to recruiting Labor candidates ahead of 2027. Locally, a Kiama CBD proposal involving the demolition of a heritage-listed property has emerged, and the government is promoting an Illawarra Shoalhaven paramedic pilot it says has kept more than 1200 people out of emergency departments.
briefing.localWatch: Kiama's CBD development debate sharpens, with the Illawarra Mercury reporting a proposal to demolish a heritage-listed property that it says is not backed by the Planning Department. On the service side, the state government is spruiking an Illawarra Shoalhaven extended care paramedic pilot and backing a science-based approach to managing the Lake Conjola entrance, while Mount Ousley interchange works bring new temporary traffic arrangements from mid-December.

stories.headline: Developer Level 33 flags plans to demolish heritage-listed property
stories.summary: The Illawarra Mercury reports that developer Level 33 has flagged a Kiama CBD development plan that includes demolishing a heritage-listed home. According to the Mercury, the proposal is not backed by the Planning Department.

stories.headline: Pilot eases pressure on Illawarra Shoalhaven emergency departments
stories.summary: The NSW Government says a NSW Ambulance pilot offering alternatives to hospital care for less urgent patients has meant more than a thousand people across the Illawarra and Shoalhaven avoided emergency departments this winter. The South Coast Register reports the figure as more than 1200 patients under the extended care paramedic trial.

stories.headline: NSW Government backs science-based Lake Conjola entrance management
stories.summary: Shoalhaven City Council reports that the NSW Government has backed a science-based approach to managing the Lake Conjola entrance. No further detail was supplied with the council's announcement.

stories.headline: Right turn across M1 to end as Mount Ousley interchange hits major milestone
stories.summary: The NSW Government says work on the Mount Ousley Interchange is progressing, with temporary traffic arrangements starting from mid-December to give crews room to continue construction. The change will end a right turn across the M1.

stories.headline: Flinders Street developments means traffic is getting worse, admits government
stories.summary: The Illawarra Mercury reports that Transport for NSW has acknowledged travel times along Flinders Street are already increasing as development in the area proceeds.

stories.headline: Rising costs made them cancel in-home aged care. Three days later, they were in hospital
stories.summary: The Illawarra Mercury reports on a new Illawarra report that it says identifies "serious implementation failures" in the Support at Home Program, which began last November. The Mercury links those findings to older residents cancelling in-home care because of cost.

stories.headline: Ex-Liberal minister eyes return to politics
stories.summary: The Australian reports that a former federal immigration minister is tipped to contest Liberal preselection for a NSW seat.

stories.headline: NSW regional and interstate trains could be offline for a week from Friday
stories.summary: The ABC reports that NSW regional and interstate passenger train services are set to be suspended for a week from Friday because of industrial action. It reports the rail network operator has warned of major disruption to freight services that will also affect supply chains.

stories.headline: Catholic takeover of 14 hospitals approved as IVF workaround announced
stories.summary: The ABC reports the NSW government will support access to surgical theatres for Hunter IVF patients, to fill a gap ahead of a proposed Catholic operator taking over 14 hospitals.

stories.headline: Mandatory lead testing of childcare centres in Broken Hill
stories.summary: The NSW government has announced mandatory lead testing at Broken Hill childcare centres and a new multi-agency committee to address high blood lead levels in children, the ABC reports.

stories.headline: A nest of fire ants with ‘multiple queens’ has been found in Sydney. Here’s what you need to know
stories.summary: Guardian Australia reports the NSW government is scaling up its fire ant response after saying a nest found at Auburn was larger and more complex than first thought. It is the second detection in Sydney this year, following one at Enfield in September.

stories.headline: 'Boys' club' culture exposed across NSW prison system
stories.summary: The ABC reports that the Independent Commission Against Corruption has identified a "boys' club" within Corrective Services NSW, in which it says sexualised language is tolerated and staff are discouraged from making complaints. The Daily Telegraph reports the ICAC findings describe a culture that protects perpetrators of sexual abuse in NSW prisons.

stories.headline: UOW rises in governance rankings despite ICAC anti-corruption scandal
stories.summary: The South Coast Register reports that the University of Wollongong has improved its position in a global governance scorecard, despite an ICAC anti-corruption matter involving the university.

stories.headline: Chris Minns doesn’t want ‘stacks, whacks and hacks’. He’s looking elsewhere for MPs
stories.summary: Writing in the Herald, the author argues Premier Chris Minns is looking outside the usual party channels when recruiting Labor candidates. The piece contends it remains reasonable for MPs and the party's ideological base to ask what a new candidate actually believes in.

stories.headline: The cost to taxpayers of Minns’ timetable backflip? Extra pay for train drivers
stories.summary: The Herald examines the cost to taxpayers of the Minns government's rail timetable reversal, reporting it involves extra pay for train drivers.

elsewhere.text: Ben Raue and William Bowe discuss the kinds of seats to watch at this weekend's Victorian election and how the count may unfold on the night.
The ABC reports the regional Victorian seat of Ripon has become a microcosm of wider voter disaffection on the eve of that state's election.
A bill to ban greyhound racing in Tasmania from 2029 has failed in the upper house, with members criticising the process begun by Premier Jeremy Rockliff, the ABC reports.
William Bowe reports a DemosAU poll has WA Labor leading 54-46, finding no lasting damage from September's Secret Harbour by-election loss.
